IncidentBot: Pager — auth-service: sudden 401 burst (12k reqs/7m). Distinct source IP cluster, odd user-agent patterns. Possible replay or token exposure. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/auth-unauthorized-spike. Incident bot id=inc-2470012345
Oncall_Jun: oncall Jun here, ack. Paging in.
Aisha: I'm taking triage. Pulling auth logs (last 15m) and S3 access logs.
Ben: I see the spike. 12k 401s over 7m, top UA includes "Mozilla/5.0 (bot) redwood-probe" and several curl agents. IPs look clustered in 3 CIDR blocks.
Marco: Any evidence of leaked full API keys in logs? Check for 'Authorization: Bearer' patterns in raw access logs. Also search S3 access logs for public-get-object events.
Aisha: quick grep shows some requests contain truncated tokens (e.g., "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-abc..."), plus a few requests to /v1/auth/replay with curl UA. I'm seeing old debug snapshots in s3://dev-logs/debug-snapshots with public-read ACL from last week. Opening S3 console now.
Priya: If logs contained token fragments we should assume leakage. Which principals use those tokens? Will we need to rotate service accounts?
Aisha: Affected principals look like: service-account-inference-prod and internal-session-cache. I recommend rotating those keys first.
Ben: Proposed immediate mitigation plan:
1) Revoke active sessions/tokens for affected principals (partial revocation to avoid mass user impact)
2) Rotate service principal keys and update secrets manager
3) Push new keys and rolling-restart affected services (auth-proxy, inference pool)
4) Apply WAF blocks on suspicious IP ranges + remove public ACL on s3://dev-logs/debug-snapshots
Who owns KMS/Secrets updates?
Oncall_Jun: I can trigger the token revokes and add temporary rate-limit blocks. @Marco can you own KMS/secret updates?
Marco: I got it. Creating new CMK and rotating secrets now. Commands I'm running:
```
# create key
aws kms create-key --description "temp-rotate-inc-2470012345" --region us-west-2
# create alias
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/inc-2470012345 --target-key-id <key-id>
# update secrets (example)
aws secretsmanager update-secret --secret-id arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-west-2:123456789012:secret:SERVICE_INFER_KEY --secret-string '{"key":"NEW_VALUE"}'
```
Marco: After updating secrets I'll trigger rolling deploys for inference pool. Planning zero-downtime restarts.
Aisha: I'm removing public ACL on s3://dev-logs/debug-snapshots and applying lifecycle policy to quarantine objects for analysis (no public access). Command: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket dev-logs --acl private`.
IncidentBot: Automated job started: /jobs/revoke_tokens run_id=rev-2470012345 (status=running).
Ben: Revoke job finished: 98% of active sessions for affected principals revoked. Gateway now requiring fresh tokens for new requests. Rolling restart auth-proxy 3/3 (rolling).
Marco: New key created and secret updated. Deploy hook kicked off to propagate to services. Confirming env var SERVICE_INFER_KEY updated in secrets manager and env on deployed pods.
Aisha: After restarts, 401 rate down to baseline. WAF rules blocking 3 CIDR blocks applied. Also put an ACL block on dev-logs bucket so no further public reads.
Elena-CS: Customer X reported failures between 03:10-03:20 UTC — likely matching this incident. I've drafted a short customer update and will send once we confirm mitigation.
Priya: Initial assessment: truncated token strings found in logs (not full keys). No confirmed data exfil of customer content. Still treat as sensitive: rotate keys, tighten S3 ACLs, and redact tokens from logs in future.
Ben: Also enabling route fallback to secondary region for inference traffic for an extra safety net and set stricter prefix caching to reduce auth-touched calls.
Oncall_Jun: Handing off immediate mitigation — system stable, traffic normalized. @Aisha @Marco please prepare timeline and collect artifacts for postmortem.
Aisha: Will collect relevant logs, S3 object snapshots, and the grep outputs into the incident bucket s3://incidents/2470012345/artifacts.
Priya: Follow-ups (action items):
- S3 ACL audit + remove public ACLs (owner: infra-security)
- Rotate remaining service keys (owner: Marco)
- Improve log redaction (owner: Ben)
- Customer comms & RCA (owner: Elena-CS)
- Update runbook to include quick-revoke script (owner: Aisha)
Elena-CS: Customer X confirms service restored. Sending the interim update now. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident resolved — id=inc-2470012345, severity=P2, duration=00:12:44, primary_mitigation=key_rotation + WAF blocks.
Oncall_Jun: Closing the page. Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 1100 UTC. Thanks all.
